inlines.text: Opus 比 Sonnet 更好吗？

blocks.text: 在我们跑的基准测试里，Claude Opus 5.5 并没有胜过 Claude Sonnet 5.5。在我们跑的 GPQA Diamond 上 Sonnet 得分更高，这是一组 198 道研究生水平的科学题（92.4% 对 90.4%）。在 τ-bench airline 上它同样更高，这是一个多轮客服智能体基准（78.7% 对 75.5%）。在 Artificial Analysis 指数上 Opus 领先 1.6 分。在我们两次运行中，Sonnet 每个任务的成本都不到一半：GPQA 每题 $0.025，Opus 是 $0.054；τ-bench 每任务 $0.16，Opus 是 $0.34。

blocks.text: Haiku 够不够格取代 Sonnet？

inlines.text: Haiku 够不够格取代 Sonnet？

blocks.text: 对于需求明确、常规性的工作，Haiku 5.5 可以取代 Sonnet。它在 τ-bench airline 上得分 76.0%，比 Opus 高半分，比 Sonnet 低 2.7 分，每任务成本 $0.011，约为 Sonnet 的十四分之一。我们每个模型跑了 100 到 200 个任务，所以这个基准上几分之差可能是噪声。在 GPQA Diamond 上 Haiku 落后 Sonnet 5.8 分，在 Artificial Analysis 指数上落后 12.6 分——该指数中智能体任务和通用知识各占 30%，编程和科学推理各占 20%。在常规编程上，我们下面的测试没有发现差距。

inlines.text: 我们的编程测试说明了什么？

blocks.text: 我们测了两件事：按规格写函数，以及用 Claude Code 修一个代码仓库。三个模型在两项测试中都通过了全部测试。

inlines.text: 我们测了两件事：按规格写函数，以及用 Claude Code 修一个代码仓库。三个模型在两项测试中都通过了全部测试。

blocks.text: 我们写了 11 个 Python 任务，每个都配一个隐藏测试文件。8 个日常任务是：解析时长、合并区间、LRU 缓存、不用 eval 的算术求值器、cron 表达式的下次运行时间、自动换行、语义化版本排序，以及 JSON 路径读取器。3 个困难任务分别是：不用 re 模块的正则引擎、带三值 NULL 逻辑的 SQL WHERE 过滤器，以及夏令时切换日跨时区的空闲日程时段。每个模型对每个日常任务作答两次、每个困难任务作答三次，使用模型默认设置，每个模型共 25 次尝试。

blocks.text:
import os
import requests
for model in ["anthropic/claude-opus-5.5", "anthropic/claude-sonnet-5.5", "anthropic/claude-haiku-5.5"]:
    r = requests.post(
        "https://openrouter.ai/api/v1/chat/completions",
        headers={"Authorization": f"Bearer {os.environ['OPENROUTER_API_KEY']}"},
        json={"model": model, "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Write a Python function that merges overlapping intervals."}]},
        timeout=300,
    )
    usage = r.json()["usage"]
    print(f"{model}: {usage['completion_tokens']} output tokens, ${usage['cost']:.4f}")

blocks.text: For most teams, the choice is between Opus and Sonnet, and the question is whether Opus is worth twice Sonnet’s price per token. On the coding tasks we tested, it wasn’t. We gave each model the same 11 coding tasks with hidden tests and the same bug-fix task in Claude Code. Every model passed everything, so what separated them was cost. Haiku was 19 to 30 times cheaper than Opus per task, and Sonnet cost between half and two-thirds as much as Opus.

inlines.text: How do Opus, Sonnet, and Haiku differ?

blocks.text: Opus 5.5, Sonnet 5.5, and Haiku 5.5 are three tiers of the same model generation. Anthropic released Opus 5.5 on September 22, 2026, Sonnet 5.5 on September 28, and Haiku 5.5 on October 7. All three have a 1-million-token context window and accept text, images, and PDFs. They differ mostly in price and, for Haiku, in lower benchmark scores.

blocks.text: On the benchmarks we run, Claude Opus 5.5 does not beat Claude Sonnet 5.5. Sonnet scored higher on our run of GPQA Diamond, a set of 198 graduate-level science questions (92.4% vs 90.4%). It also scored higher on τ-bench airline, a multi-turn customer-service agent benchmark (78.7% vs 75.5%). Opus leads by 1.6 points on the Artificial Analysis index. On both of our runs, Sonnet costs less than half as much per task, at $0.025 per GPQA question against $0.054 and $0.16 per τ-bench task against $0.34.

blocks.text: Is Haiku good enough to replace Sonnet?

inlines.text: Is Haiku good enough to replace Sonnet?

blocks.text: Haiku 5.5 can replace Sonnet for well-specified, routine work. It scored 76.0% on τ-bench airline, half a point above Opus and 2.7 points behind Sonnet, at $0.011 per task. That is about a fourteenth of Sonnet’s cost. Our runs had 100 to 200 tasks per model, so gaps of a few points on this benchmark may be noise. Haiku trails Sonnet by 5.8 points on GPQA Diamond and by 12.6 points on the Artificial Analysis index, which weights agentic tasks and general knowledge at 30% each and coding and scientific reasoning at 20% each. On routine coding, our tests below found no gap.

blocks.text: What did our coding tests show?

inlines.text: What did our coding tests show?

blocks.text: We tested two things, writing a function to a spec and fixing a repo with Claude Code. All three models passed every test in both.

inlines.text: We tested two things, writing a function to a spec and fixing a repo with Claude Code. All three models passed every test in both.

blocks.text: We wrote 11 Python tasks, each with a hidden test file. The eight everyday tasks were parsing durations, merging intervals, an LRU cache, an arithmetic evaluator without eval, the next run time of a cron expression, word wrapping, Semantic Versioning sort order, and a JSON path reader. The three hard tasks were a regex engine without the re module, a SQL WHERE filter with three-valued NULL logic, and free calendar slots across time zones on daylight-saving transition days. Each model answered each everyday task twice and each hard task three times, with the models’ default settings, for 25 attempts per model.

blocks.text: We serve all three models through one API, one key, and one request format, so switching means changing the model string. This loop sends the same prompt to each tier and prints the output tokens and the cost we return on every response.

blocks.text:
import os
import requests
for model in ["anthropic/claude-opus-5.5", "anthropic/claude-sonnet-5.5", "anthropic/claude-haiku-5.5"]:
    r = requests.post(
        "https://openrouter.ai/api/v1/chat/completions",
        headers={"Authorization": f"Bearer {os.environ['OPENROUTER_API_KEY']}"},
        json={"model": model, "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Write a Python function that merges overlapping intervals."}]},
        timeout=300,
    )
    usage = r.json()["usage"]
    print(f"{model}: {usage['completion_tokens']} output tokens, ${usage['cost']:.4f}")

inlines.text: Is Claude Haiku cheaper than Sonnet?

blocks.text: Yes. On OpenRouter, Haiku 5.5 costs 20 times less per input and output token than Claude Sonnet 5.5 for prompts under 100,000 tokens, at $0.10 per million input tokens against $2.00. In our Claude Code runs the gap per session was smaller, about 12 times, partly because Haiku took more turns to reach the same result.
